headline: Maine CDC confirms measles case in Somerset County adult
dek: The state says the unvaccinated adult’s case is Maine’s first reported since February and identifies a possible exposure window in Waterville.
body: Maine health officials confirmed a measles case in an unvaccinated adult from Somerset County, the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention said in a Sept. 16 advisory.

The agency said the case was confirmed Sept. 15 and that investigators were working to identify and notify people who may have been exposed. Maine Public reported that the case is the first reported in the state since five cases were confirmed in February.

Maine CDC identified MaineGeneral Express Care at 211 Main Street in Waterville as a potential exposure location on Sept. 12 between 8 and 11 a.m. The agency said that window could change as the investigation continues.

People who may have been exposed should review their measles immunity and monitor for symptoms, including fever, cough, runny nose, red or watery eyes and rash. Maine CDC advises anyone who develops symptoms to contact a health care provider before arriving at a clinic or hospital so staff can limit possible spread.
